report.verdict: An emergency department nurse manager whose profile connects staffing decisions to patient flow and nurse retention.
write_up: You lead an emergency department at a Level II trauma center, and your profile makes the work clear. It gives a recruiter reasons to remember you: changes to triage, nurse retention and a $14.5M labor budget. Your profile isn't likely to be the reason someone moves on, though the needs of a particular role and competition still matter.

The Saguaro Valley Medical Center manager job is the model for the rest. It names the department you lead, the changes you made and what happened afterward. Your About also brings the triage work right to the top.

If you want to round out the profile, start with the Desert Ridge bedside job: name the patients and care you handled there. For a future director-level conversation, you could also add any budget planning beyond the ED. A recruiter can already see the manager work without guessing.

cards.line: Bedside care in a 28-bed community ED.
cards.cannot_tell: Bedside care tells me where you worked, but not which patients you cared for or what that care involved. One line about the work would round out your nursing background.
cards.example: Bedside care in a 28-bed community ED, including [types of patients and care you provided].
cards.question: What types of patients did you care for at Desert Ridge, and what nursing care did you provide?

cards.where: Saguaro Valley Medical Center, Nurse Manager description
cards.line: Cut left-without-being-seen from 5.1% to 2.3% in two years with front-door triage and a new overflow plan.
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this line. It connects the triage and overflow changes to a specific change in patients leaving before being seen.

cards.where: Saguaro Valley Medical Center, Nurse Manager description
cards.line: Own a $14.5M labor budget; finished the last two fiscal years within 1% of plan.
cards.cannot_tell: The budget line is strong. For a director-level role, a recruiter may also look for budget planning beyond the ED, if that has been part of your work.
cards.example: Own a $14.5M labor budget; [your part in budget planning beyond the ED, if applicable].
cards.question: What part, if any, have you had in budget planning beyond the ED?

fit.why: Your headline and current job name emergency department management, and your descriptions show staffing, patient flow and budget work.
fit.level: manager, you lead a 42-bed ED with 96 nurses and techs
fit.note: 'Emergency Department Nurse Manager' is in your headline. 'Nurse Staffing' and 'Trauma Care' are in your top skills. 'Split-flow' is in your About. 'Quality improvement' and 'capital budgeting' are not on your profile; they are optional terms if they describe your work.
